nodes.name: W precursor synthesis
nodes.procedure: 3 g of polydopamine (PDA), 3 g of P123, 0.5 g of Tris, 0.6 g of Na2H2PO4·2H2O, and 0.04 g of Na2WO4·2H2O were dissolved in distilled water (30 mL), then one piece of Ni foam was immersed into the mixture solution with continuous stirring for 6 h. The flower-like W precursors were then collected by centrifugation, washed with a mixture of distilled water and ethanol, and then dried at 60 °C.

nodes.characterization_summary: W content in W-ACs determined to be 10.49 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: according to the coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis, the weight ratio of W atoms in W-ACs was determined to be of 10.49 wt%

nodes.characterization_summary: W-SAs and W-ACs show only carbon substrate peaks at 21.3° and 43.5° with no tungsten crystalline phases; WC NPs show additional peak at 31.5° for (001) WC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD patterns of W-SAs and W-ACs only contain peaks corresponding to the underlying carbon substrates (i.e., 21.3 and 43.5°) with no signals indicating tungsten-containing crystal phases. In contrast, an additional peak at 31.5° is obtained in WC NPs

nodes.characterization_summary: W-SAs and W-ACs show D (1341 cm⁻¹) and G (1585 cm⁻¹) carbon bands; WC NPs show additional W-C stretching at ~800 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectra of W-SAs and W-ACs, only peaks at around 1341 and 1585 cm⁻¹... whereas WC NPs show a broad band corresponding to the W-C stretching mode at around 800 cm⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ variable-temperature NAP-XPS (H2, 0.1 mbar) monitors W 4f evolution from W-SAs (W-C peaks 31.5/33.6 eV) through W-AC formation (highest W-C intensity at 550°C) to WC NPs; W-ACs at 580°C show Pt-like valence band with high d-band density of states near Fermi level.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the W 4f XPS core-level signals were recorded at temperatures ranging from 400 to 600 °C (Fig. 2b)... the highest intensities of W-C signals with sharp peaks were detected in the sample treated at 550 °C... the tungsten species treated at 580 °C have the most favorable Pt-like electronic structure regarding both the density of states and peak features near the Fermi level.

nodes.characterization_summary: W-SAs lack W-W coordination; W-ACs show clear but weak W-W at ~2.85 Å and dominant W-C/O (1-2 Å); WC NPs show strong W-W.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the reference sample of W foil exhibits typical scattering path of W-W coordination at 2.85 Å, which is almost absent in that of W-SAs... W-W coordination is clear in W-ACs... much weaker than that of WC NPs

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl: W-ACs 155.7 mF/cm², W-SAs 26 mF/cm², WC NPs 18 mF/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: an obvious increase in the Cdl (155.7 mF/cm²) was obtained for the W-ACs sample... Compared to the well-dispersed isolated W sites in W-SAs (26 mF/cm²) and crystallized WC NPs (18 mF/cm²)

nodes.characterization_summary: W-ACs show charge transfer resistance of ~12 Ω, smaller than P-doped C, WC NPs, and W-SAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the charge transfer resistance for W-ACs catalyzed alkaline HER process was determined to be approximately 12 Ω, which is much smaller than those of P-doped C, WC NPs and W-SAs

nodes.characterization_summary: All tungsten species show higher white-line intensities than W foil indicating oxidation states; adsorption edge shifts to lower energies from W-SAs to WC NPs indicating reduced valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white-line intensities for all tungsten species are higher than that of the W foil reference... The adsorption edge position exhibit a negative shift towards lower energies from W-SAs to WC NPs
